items.title: Tuanku Muhriz: Customs cannot be defended by breaching the rules
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Ibni Almarhum Tuanku Munawir today said customs cannot be defended by breaking the very rules of custom, in a pointed address directed at those who have disputed the rules of succession in recent months. Speaking at Istana Besar Seri Menanti this afternoon to mark the investiture of the 17th Undang of Luak Jelebu, Tuanku Muhriz said Negeri Sembilan’s constitutional monarchy, adat and legal provisions must be upheld together. Disputes must follow custom and law The Yamtuan further said the customary system must continue to be strengthened to remain relevant with the times, without neglecting its founding principles and rules.

items.title: Public Services Commission awaits circular on RM2,500 starting salary for fresh grads entering public service
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 14 — The implementation of the RM2,500 starting salary for fresh graduates entering the public service, announced in Budget 2027, is pending an official circular outlining the implementation details. Malaysian Public Services Commission (SPA) chairman and Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the details would include the implementation timeline and related payment components. Asked whether the RM2,500 amount included other allowances, Ahmad Jailani said the matter would be reviewed and clarified in the official circular.

items.title: Malaysia gives Nepal US$1m in flood relief aid
items.summary: Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan presented the contribution to Nepal’s Chargé d’Affaires in Kuala Lumpur, Mudita Bajracharya, at a ceremony here on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra. “The contribution reflects Malaysia’s unwavering support for the government and people of Nepal during this difficult time,” Wisma Putra said in a statement. “The new ordinance will provide greater legal and administrative certainty for affected families,” Wisma Putra said.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Pahang to reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka and Pahang will reopen tomorrow. The Selangor State Education Department said school operations in the state will prioritise the safety, health and well-being of pupils and school staff. The Melaka State Education Department said educational institutions under MOE will resume operations tomorrow, pending official confirmation of the latest API readings.

items.title: Parliament’s new service council to be fully operational by December, says Dewan Rakyat Speaker
items.summary: Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said the council would oversee matters including the service scheme, career paths and administration of parliamentary officers, as well as ensure compliance with the provisions of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025. The event was attended by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Dewan Negara President Senator Datuk Seri Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. The four appointees, comprising two government and two opposition representatives, are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor), Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam), Datuk Seri Dr Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu).

items.title: Weather warning: MetMalaysia puts most of the country on thunderstorm alert
items.summary: Perak faces widespread disruption across Kerian, Selama, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, and Bagan Datuk. Across Selangor, the warning blankets Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Hulu Langat, and Sepang. Across East Malaysia, the warning stretches across multiple divisions in Sarawak.

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial: Prosecution cites contradictions in four accused’s defence
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 14 — The High Court here was told today that there are four main grounds for the prosecution’s bid to convict the four accused in the murder of teenager T. Nhaveen nine years ago, with the contention that the defence failed to raise reasonable doubt against its case. Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Amril Johari said among these grounds was the contradiction between the defence’s version during the prosecution’s case and the accused’s testimony at the defence stage last week. “The defence’s case at the prosecution stage is totally different from the defence now.

items.title: Five govt buildings get solar installations ahead of schedule, says works minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Five grid-connected photovoltaic (GCPV) solar installation projects at government buildings have been completed ahead of schedule, with a combined installed capacity of 779.86 kilowatts, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said. He said the Public Works Department (JKR) had also implemented grid-connected photovoltaic and off-grid solar installations involving 46 Federal Government buildings, 283 rural schools in Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, four Royal Malaysia Police border posts and an Orang Asli village. As of last September, eight projects involving 23 buildings with a capacity of 5.8 megawatts had completed their Defects Liability Period (DLP), while seven projects involving 11 buildings with a capacity of 2.09 megawatts remained within the period.

items.title: Sarawak Education Dept: Schools open tomorrow, outdoor activities halted if API tops 100
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 14 — All schools and educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Sarawak will operate as usual tomorrow, despite the ongoing haze affecting several areas in the state. In a statement today, the Sarawak Education Department (JPN) said schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeded 100 must suspend all outdoor activities. “Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure amid the current haze situation.

items.title: Why should a good man go when the corrupt stay? Anwar says Malaysia needs ministers like Anthony Loke
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim sought again today to make a case for Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook to remain in his Cabinet, saying the country needs principled leaders and that the corrupt should be the ones stepping down. Speaking at the Transport Ministry during the distribution of RM1,000 special financial assistance to taxi, rental car, and school bus drivers, Anwar commended Loke's dedication to ordinary working Malaysians, including the initiative today. Loke, who is the DAP secretary-general, tendered his resignation as transport minister on September 19 following the political controversy surrounding the conditional royal pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.

items.title: MACC: Fighting corruption starts with rejecting bribes, reporting misconduct
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Deputy Chief Commissioner (Prevention) Datuk Azmi Kamaruzaman said building a corruption-free culture starts with honest decisions and firm personal convictions, supported by sustained commitment from all parties. He was speaking at the launch of the “Program Langkah Merdeka 118, Bersama Perangi Rasuah” programme, held in conjunction with the MACC’s 59th anniversary celebration for Kuala Lumpur at Stadium Merdeka here today. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib said the symbolic act of carrying and hoisting the MACC flag atop Merdeka 118, Malaysia’s tallest building and the world’s second tallest, reflected the commission’s determination to elevate the anti-corruption agenda and strengthen integrity without compromise.

items.title: Paddy farmers who suffered yield losses from fertiliser delays may get targeted aid, says minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The government will assess whether to provide targeted assistance to paddy farmers whose yields declined due to delays in fertiliser supplies, evaluating affected cases on a case-by-case basis. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the assessment would identify farmers who genuinely suffered losses before considering any assistance. In a separate development, Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said 10 per cent of the funds collected through the Warriors’ Fund Campaign (KTP) had been allocated for investment in fixed deposits with financial institutions.

items.title: Foreign minister: Malaysians in Riyadh, Jeddah safe amid Saudi tensions
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysians living and working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, have been reported safe amid continuing tensions in the country, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. He said daily reports from the Malaysian Embassy in Riyadh and the Malaysian Consulate in Jeddah confirmed that Malaysians in both cities were safe and well. He said the security situation in Saudi Arabia remained tense following another reported attack yesterday.

items.title: Johor JPJ seeks p-hailing operators’ help to curb repeat offences, especially running red lights
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 14 — The Johor Road Transport Department (JPJ) will meet p-hailing operators to discuss measures to raise riders’ awareness of road safety and curb repeat traffic offences, particularly running red lights. State JPJ director Zulkarnain Yasin said the department had received numerous complaints about traffic offences involving p-hailing riders, particularly running red lights, captured in dashboard camera footage. He said JPJ also imposed demerit points on road users who repeatedly committed offences such as running red lights, in addition to issuing summonses.

items.title: Budget 2027: Tengku Zafrul urges local semiconductor firms to move up value chain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Local semiconductor companies must translate Budget 2027’s allocation into greater participation in higher-value activities such as integrated circuit (IC) design, as Malaysia seeks to strengthen its position in the global semiconductor supply chain, said Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. Speaking on Bernama TV’s The Nation programme, the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman said Malaysia has developed a mature semiconductor ecosystem over more than five decades but needs to move beyond its traditional strengths in assembly and testing to capture greater value from the industry. Tengku Zafrul said the measures would help Malaysian companies strengthen their capabilities and move further up the value chain.

items.title: 1MDB trial: Judge rejects Najib’s bid to stay prison sentence, says his medical issues not special circumstances
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The High Court today dismissed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application to stay the execution of his 15-year prison sentence and RM11.38 billion fine in the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) corruption case. Delivering her decision, High Court Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin held that the gravity of the offences and overarching public interest considerations outweighed the applicant's private grievances. “Having weighed the competing interests of the applicant against public interest considerations, the court does not agree that the medical issues raised satisfy the special circumstances test,” the judge said.

items.title: Damansara mini tornado caused by active thunderstorm clouds, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The mini tornado or landspout that struck Damansara, Selangor, yesterday evening was caused by active thunderstorm clouds (cumulonimbus), said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. Mohd Hisham said tornadoes in Malaysia occur only on a relatively small scale, measuring less than 10 metres and lasting for a very short time. Mohd Hisham said landspouts, tornadoes over land and waterspouts over the sea occur frequently during the monsoon transition phase, from March to May and September to October.

items.title: Man drives SUV 130m down train tracks in Port Klang, police say KTMB investigating
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 14 — A 60-year-old motorist drove his SUV onto railway tracks and travelled roughly 130 metres before coming to a stop at a KTMB station in Pelabuhan Klang, police confirmed today. The late-night incident occurred around 11.40pm on Oct 11 at a level crossing near the Jalan Limbungan KTMB station, Klang South district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said in a statement today. “According to preliminary police investigations, the driver, a Kuala Lumpur resident, was heading home when his vehicle strayed onto the tracks,” Lim said.

items.title: King attends 273rd Conference of Rulers at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers meeting at Istana Negara, chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah. Present were the Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail; Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah; Sultan of Kedah, Al-Aminul Karim Sultan Sallehuddin Sultan Badlishah; and Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah. The Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail; Crown Prince of Kelantan, Tengku Muhammad Fakhry Petra; and Tunku Temenggong of Johor, Tunku Idris Iskandar Sultan Ibrahim, also attended.

items.title: Anwar hails Parliamentary Services Act as key reform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim described the implementation of the Parliamentary Services Act 2025 as a key step by the MADANI Government towards fulfilling its reform pledge to the people, including limiting powers traditionally held by the government. He said the move was a key pillar of the country’s reform agenda, reflecting the government’s commitment to strengthening Parliament’s independence and advancing the maturity of the country’s parliamentary democracy. “I consider this change and the Parliamentary Services Act important because they give meaning to parliamentary democracy and reflect the maturity of our democratic system.

items.title: MPS urges Putrajaya to detail contract pharmacists’ absorption timeline and quota numbers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Malaysian Pharmacists Society (MPS) has welcomed the government’s move to recommend contract pharmacy officers for permanent posts, but insists Putrajaya must quickly settle the critical details on quota figures, eligibility rules, and an implementation timeline. The response follows remarks by Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, who confirmed on Monday that the Ministry of Health (MOH) will submit a proposal to the Ministry of Finance and the Cabinet to absorb contract pharmacy officers into permanent positions. He said permanent posts for dental and pharmacy personnel will come from a distinct allocation, separate from the 9,000 permanent medical officer positions unveiled under Budget 2027.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah records strongest economic growth in six years
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 14 — Sabah’s economy grew by 5.1 per cent last year, its strongest performance in six years, with gross domestic product (GDP) reaching RM88.8 billion, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. “Sabah has momentum. Hajiji said the state’s record development ceiling of RM12.02 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan, covering 933 new projects and 240 extension projects, would further strengthen Sabah’s competitiveness and attractiveness to investors.

items.title: Former e-hailing driver in JB gets eight years’ jail for making toddler eat faeces
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 —A former e-hailing driver was sentenced to eight years and six months’ imprisonment by the High Court in Johor Bahru today for abusing a three-year-old boy in 2022, which included forcing the child to eat his own excrement. Chan Wen Jie, 32, pleaded guilty before Judicial Commissioner Datuk Abdul Fareed Abdul Gafoor to an alternative charge of child abuse under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, FMT reported. “Forcing the child to eat faeces was a cruel and degrading act that could in no way be considered a form of discipline.

items.title: Tengku Zafrul: Malaysia should assess investors by job quality, treatment of women
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Investors in Malaysia should be assessed on the quality of jobs they create and how they treat workers, particularly women, said Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) chairman Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz. He said fair wages, safe workplaces and flexible working arrangements should be key criteria for quality investments. He said greater workforce participation by women, alongside equal access to capital and markets for women entrepreneurs, would expand the economy’s productive capacity.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia begin talks on joint action against forest fires causing haze, says Tok Mat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 14 — Malaysia and Indonesia have begun discussions to explore ways of working together to tackle forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that have caused transboundary haze. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the discussions involved relevant agencies and ministries from both countries, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Foreign Ministry and the National Security Council (MKN). “Alhamdulillah, both countries, through their respective agencies and foreign ministries, will explore ways to cooperate and help address the forest fires together,” he said.

items.title: Air quality deteriorates in 28 areas; Klang Valley, Johor hotspots rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Air quality slipped further this afternoon, with 28 of the country's 68 monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 2pm, according to the Department of Environment (DOE). Another 38 stations reported moderate air quality, while two recorded good levels. All three Melaka stations were unhealthy, led by Bukit Rambai at 173.

items.title: Children without citizenship eligible for school if one parent is Malaysian, says Sarawak minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 14 — Children who do not yet hold Malaysian citizenship remain eligible for access to education at government or government-aided schools if they have at least one biological parent who is a Malaysian citizen, subject to the conditions and procedures of the Education Ministry (MOE). Sarawak Minister of Women, Childhood and Community Wellbeing Development Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah said this eligibility is governed by the Education Act 1996 (Act 550), the Education Regulations 1998 and MOE procedures currently in force. “Citizenship status and access to education are two separate matters,” she said during the question-and-answer session at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly sitting here today.

items.title: King receives courtesy visit from Melaka governor ahead of Conference of Rulers meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today received a courtesy visit from Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam at Istana Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The meeting took place before His Majesty attended the 273rd Conference of Rulers. The 273rd Conference of Rulers is chaired by the Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah.

items.title: Thick smoke seen near DUKE Highway traced to burning streetlight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — Thick smoke seen near the Duta-Ulu Kelang Expressway (DUKE), beyond the Sentul Toll Plaza on Wednesday, is believed to have been caused by a burning streetlight. Sentul district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said inspections by police and DUKE highway management found that the smoke originated from a streetlight that had caught fire, according to a report by Sinar Harian . A video showing thick smoke engulfing the area near the highway had earlier gone viral on social media.

items.title: Takiyuddin, Kiandee among four MPs appointed to Parliamentary Service Council
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 14 — The Dewan Rakyat today approved a motion by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to appoint four lawmakers to the first Parliamentary Service Council established under the Parliamentary Service Act 2025. The four lawmakers are Ramkarpal Singh (PH-Bukit Gelugor) and Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad (BN-Simpang Renggam) from the government benches, and Datuk Seri Ronald Kiandee (PN-Beluran) and Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) from the Opposition. Under Section 3(2)(f) of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025, the power to nominate members rests with the Committee of Selection.
